theater: Finland Post-Glacial Rebound, Boreal Peatlands & Lake Ice (Kvarken, Saimaa, Päijänne, Siikaneva, Halti)
compliance: Rule e2s-014 Certified (Zero Synthetic Noise, Authentic GFS Tensors, Explicit origin='upper')

fi_kvarken_vaasa.name: Kvarken Archipelago / Vaasa
fi_kvarken_vaasa.significance: UNESCO World Heritage post-glacial land uplift epicenter (~8.5-9.0 mm/yr); rapid coastal shoaling and De Geer moraine emergence.

fi_saimaa_lake.name: Lake Saimaa (Savonlinna / Linnansaari)
fi_saimaa_lake.significance: Largest labyrinthine freshwater lake system (4400 km²); winter congelation ice freeze-thaw transition and ringed seal breeding habitat.

fi_paijanne_lake.name: Lake Päijänne (Jyväskylä / Tehi)
fi_paijanne_lake.significance: Deepest lake basin in Finland (95m depth); critical freshwater aqueduct reservoir for Helsinki metropolitan region and seasonal ice breakup.

fi_siikaneva_peatland.name: Siikaneva Boreal Peatland Complex
fi_siikaneva_peatland.significance: Pristine southern raised bog complex; seasonal peat column breathing (20-45 mm elastic swelling), water table fluctuations, and carbon flux monitoring.

fi_martimoaapa_mire.name: Martimoaapa Aapa Mire / Kemi
fi_martimoaapa_mire.significance: Extensive sub-arctic aapa mire system with flark-string patterned fens; active-layer freeze-thaw decorrelation (gamma < 0.35) and snowmelt saturation.

fi_halti_lapland.name: Halti Fell / Kilpisjärvi
fi_halti_lapland.significance: Highest point in Finland (1324m); Arctic-alpine permafrost palsa mires, high-relief orographic tropospheric delay, and permafrost slope stability.
